records.text: Washington County Sheriff Nate Brooksby abruptly resigned during an election, leaving one candidate, and his name was removed from the sheriff's website and social accounts without a public explanation.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It is. So this is interesting. Sheriff Nate Brooksby has resigned suddenly. He had like a COVID resignation, died suddenly, resigned suddenly. ... He resigned and now there's an interim sheriff in place and there's like I said they're in the middle of an election so now they're down to a single candidate. ... The resignation occurred on Friday and there has not been a public statement given for this out of nowhere resignation but over the weekend his name was quietly removed from the sheriff's office website and social media pages and there was a lot of speculation and I saw that some people said that there was going to be more information that was coming out.

verification.notes: The Washington County Sheriff's Office confirms Brooksby resigned on Friday, March 27, during the scheduled sheriff election, with an acting sheriff installed. The official notice was published March 30. The claims that his name was quietly scrubbed, that only one candidate remained, and that no explanation existed are not all established by the official source.

records.speaker: Spencer Cox

appearances.snippet: On the evening of September 11th, A family member of Tyler Robinson reached out to a family friend who contacted the Washington County Sheriff's Office with information that Robinson had confessed to them or implied that he had committed the incident. ... This information was relayed to the Utah County Sheriff's Office and on-scene investigators at Utah Valley University. This information was also conveyed to the FBI.

verification.notes: Utah's criminal information says Robinson's parents believed he matched the suspect, Robinson implied he was the shooter, and a retired-deputy family friend helped arrange surrender. It also records alleged admissions to his roommate. This substantially supports the official summary quoted in context, while all guilt claims remain allegations.

records.text: Candace Owens said public records conflict on Tyler Robinson's arrival time: Sheriff Nate Brooksby said 9 p.m., while search warrants said 10:26 p.m.

verification.notes: Public sources confirm the discrepancy. Brooksby said Robinson arrived shortly before 9 p.m.; a search-warrant affidavit states approximately 2226 hours, or 10:26 p.m.

records.text: Washington County Sheriff's Office stated that surveillance footage responsive to a request concerning Tyler Robinson was no longer available after its 30-day retention period
records.speaker: Washington County Sheriff's Office

appearances.snippet: The response: "Our office does not have any applicable records responsive to this request, as the surveillance footage is no longer available after the 30-day retention period."

verification.notes: Confirmed by multiple news sources. 2News filed GRAMA request with Washington County Sheriff's Office for surveillance video of Tyler Robinson turning himself in. Sheriff's Office responded: 'Our office does not have any applicable records responsive to this request, as the surveillance footage is no longer available after the 30-day retention period.' Sheriff's office confirmed footage was never shared with any law enforcement agency. Sources: https://kutv.com/news/2news-investigates/2news-investigates-discovers-possible-missing-evidence-in-charlie-kirk-murder-case and https://cbs12.com/news/nation-world/possible-missing-evidence-in-charlie-kirk-murder-case-discovered-washington-county-tyler-robinson-turning-point-usa-surveillance-video-utah-rifle
